Quarto's Word output loses the front matter that matters in a manuscript: authors on one line with superscript affiliation numbers, a numbered affiliations list, a correspondence line, and a logo above the title.
A `reference-doc` cannot bring them back, because it controls styles rather than structure.

`better-word` supplies a custom OpenXML template instead, so the document itself is built the way a manuscript expects.

[See one rendered by this site](preview.docx).

## Starting a document

```bash
quarto use template {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

## Adding it to a document you already have

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

## Quick start

```yaml
format:
  better-word-docx: default
author:
  - name:
      given: Ada
      family: Lovelace
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000
    email: ada@example.org
    corresponding: true
    affiliations:
      - ref: inst
affiliations:
  - id: inst
    name: Example Institute
    city: London
    country: United Kingdom
```

The author model is Quarto's own [author and affiliation schema](https://quarto.org/docs/journals/authors.html#author-metadata), so nothing special has to be learned for it.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for the front matter behind the rendered document.

## Where it works

Word, through Pandoc's OpenXML template support, which needs Pandoc 3.2.1 or later.
